notes.1: Many candidates appreciated that the release of energy from nutrient molecules is respiration. Some candidates incorrectly selected nutrition.
notes.2: Many candidates correctly selected the monocotyledon, option D . Monocotyledons can be identified because their flower parts are in multiples of three. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2022
notes.3: Many candidates correctly identified the labelled structures that would also be found in an animal cell, namely W (the nucleus) and X (the cell membrane). Some candidates incorrectly selected Z (the cell wall).
notes.6: Many candidates correctly identified the cell membrane as the partially permeable membrane. Some candidates incorrectly opted for the cell wall.
notes.7: Few candidates appreciated that both starch and glycogen are made of glucose molecules.
notes.8: Few candidates understood the structure of DNA and correctly selected option B .
notes.13: A significant proportion of candidates did not know that the nutrient required to prevent scurvy is vitamin C.
notes.14: Few candidates correctly selected option B as the diagram that represents the action of lipase.
notes.15: Many candidates were able to identify the xylem in the cross-section of part of a leaf. Some candidates incorrectly opted for the palisade mesophyll cells.
notes.16: Only a minority of candidates understood which cells water must pass through to reach the xylem. Some candidates incorrectly believed that water must enter the phloem before reaching the xylem.
notes.17: While most candidates appreciated that the right side of the heart receives deoxygenated blood from the body, some candidates incorrectly believed that the right side of the heart pumps oxygenated blood to the lungs.
notes.18: Most candidates did not recognise the cell as a phagocyte that engulfs pathogens.
notes.20: Only a minority of candidates were able to identify the correct action of muscles during inspiration.
notes.21: This proved to be a challenging question for most candidates. Candidates could have derived the answer from their knowledge of the chemical equation of respiration. Since one molecule of glucose yields six molecules of carbon dioxide, then three molecules of glucose yield eighteen molecules of carbon dioxide.
notes.23: Many candidates understood that urea travels from the liver cells to the kidneys where it is filtered out of the blood. Some candidates incorrectly believed that urea is made in the kidneys. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2022
notes.25: Many candidates correctly selected option A , the fovea. However, a significant number incorrectly selected option B , the blind spot.
notes.26: Only a minority of candidates understood that the plant hormone 2,4-D is used for killing weeds.
notes.29: Few candidates understood that FSH and LH are required for the development and release of an egg cell.
notes.30: Only a minority of candidates were able to deduce that the allele for orange eyes is recessive.
notes.32: Candidates needed to read the question carefully as it asked for the chance of a male child being colour-blind. For male children, there is a 50% chance.
notes.33: Few candidates appreciated that heterozygous individuals are more resistant to malaria.
notes.36: Many candidates were unfamiliar with the definition of a population and could not apply it to the context in the question.
notes.37: Only a minority of candidates understood that all kingdoms share the same genetic code. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology June 2022
